findings.summary: The vectors test Zlib alone for only 5 of A1's 8 kinds and 2 custodies. The rule claims every component, kind and custody, and the brief asks for each kind.
findings.evidence: The 25 cases have Zlib alone as CRATE, ARTIFACT, HOST_OS_LIBRARY, STATIC_SYSTEM_LIBRARY (linked into a REPOSITORY_BUILT binary) and PLANEON_SOURCE. There is no case for GO_MODULE, UPSTREAM_BINARY or HOST_OS_PROGRAM. There is none with custody COMPOSITE_REVIEW_REQUIRED or TENANT_ATTESTED_PINNED (the base's other custodies), and none for a legacy crate field alone. amendment.json:50 and README.md:34 claim DEFAULT_ALLOWED 'for every component, kind and custody'. The behaviour itself is right. A differential probe ran 338 cases: 17 templates x 8 kinds x 2 custodies, plus nft, glibc, libnftnl, gmp and libpathrs. Zlib under A2 matched the base default-allowed term W3C-20150513 (same sort position) under A1, with 0 mismatches. So only the recorded evidence is missing. Fix: add Zlib alone for the 3 missing kinds and the 2 missing custodies, and optionally as a crate field. Then have check require a DEFAULT_ALLOWED 'Zlib' case for every entry of a1.KINDS.

findings.summary: The phoenix-sqlean effect leaves out that RA-LICENSE-001's model reads the base lists directly, so simply re-running it still gives DENY_UNKNOWN_LICENSE. The consumer non-claim names only A1 consumers.
findings.evidence: scripts/research_adoption_v3.py reads legal/third-party-license-policy.yaml itself: POLICY_PATH at line 34, defaultAllowedSpdx parsed at line 212, the read at line 271. It consumes neither A1 nor A2. tests/test_research_adoption_v3.py:881-882 pin ['MIT','Zlib'] -> DENY_UNKNOWN_LICENSE, and the v3 profile refuses a changed policy file. README.md:67-68 ('A later research-adoption revision re-runs its check and decides the ceiling') and amendment.json notClaimed[1] read as if re-running the check is enough. notClaimed[2] and README.md:85-86 say only that A1 consumers adopt A2 later. The effect under A2's classifier (DEFAULT_ALLOWED) is stated correctly. The research record is byte-identical: git diff 5e83b257..60472192 adds only the five subject files. Fix: say that consumers reading the base directly, RA-LICENSE-001's model included, keep Zlib UNKNOWN until they adopt the A2 overlay. Say that the later revision must classify with A2, not only re-run, to reach DEFAULT_ALLOWED. The research record needs no change.

findings.summary: The guard 'a result changes only through an added term' is not exact: _leaves strips ' WITH <exception>', and line 180 also exempts any A2 REFUSED. So README.md:59-60's claim fails for WITH forms.
findings.evidence: _leaves('Zlib WITH LLVM-exception', False) returns {'Zlib'}. Under exact matching the term is 'Zlib WITH LLVM-exception', and README.md:42-43 says it stays UNKNOWN. Probe M7 (in memory): the A2 policy was drifted to also make 'Zlib WITH LLVM-exception' DEFAULT_ALLOWED, and vector 9 was changed to expect that. check ACCEPTED it, and both guards (line 157 and lines 180-181) let it through. Line 180's 'or a2 REFUSED' exemption is never needed, because A1 and A2 share the parser and so refuse the same expressions. It does let an accepted-to-refused change through, and line 157 has no such exemption. Fix: collect whole leaf strings (found.add(item)) and drop the REFUSED exemption. Optionally require each added term to be a bare SPDX license id. Probe M6: a compound added term 'Zlib OR SSPL-1.0' passes the overlap checks and is refused only by the vectors.

findings.summary: check hashes one read of each A1 file but uses another: the A1 replay parses an unhashed third read, and the A1 classifier that runs is the imported module, not the hashed bytes.
findings.evidence: Reads in one check: A1 vectors 3, A1 record 2, base 2, A1 model 1 (hashed only). Pins are computed on the second read (line 135), and the replay parses a third read (line 154). Probe M8: a reader that returns a one-case A1 vectors file on the third read was ACCEPTED, so the replay covered 1 case, not 88. Likewise, a1._check validates the A1 record from a different read than the one pinned. The classifier that runs is whatever 'import license_amendment' resolves to. scripts/safe_yaml.py, which A1 uses to parse the base, is not pinned. This is closed if the packet layer's reader re-checks every read against its era digests and loads the pinned A1 module bytes, as the 223 layer's _verified does (round-2 P1-F4). Hence NOTE. Optional fix: in _check, read each path once, then hash and parse the same bytes.

findings.summary: 'What A2 changes' names only the approved-review election change. A2 also changes elections against an exception expression, open content and the A1 class, and accepts an OR whose other choice needs review. No case covers these.
findings.evidence: Differential probe, A1 -> A2 on the same expression: 'Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception OR Zlib' elects Zlib instead of the exception expression (rank 1 before rank 2). 'CC0-1.0 OR Zlib' for an ARTIFACT elects Zlib instead of the open-content term. 'GPL-2.0-or-later OR Zlib' for libnftnl and 'LGPL-2.1-or-later OR Zlib' for glibc linked into runc elect Zlib instead of the class term. 'Zlib OR GPL-3.0-only' goes from OPTIONAL_EXPLICIT_REVIEW to ACCEPTED_OR. All of these follow A1's ranking and OR-choice rules, so they are correct. Listing them, with a case or two, would complete the stated effect.

findings.summary: The near-miss notes rest on the policy's exact matching, not on licence identity. SPDX matches licence ids case-insensitively, and the SPDX list spells the acknowledgement variant with a lowercase z.
findings.evidence: This rests on my own knowledge of the SPDX specification (Annex D) and the SPDX licence list, not checked online (no network). SPDX matches licence identifiers case-insensitively, so 'zlib' names the same licence as 'Zlib'. The policy's EXACT_SPDX_EXPRESSION makes it UNKNOWN. That fails closed and matches the base, where 'mit' is UNKNOWN too. Vector 6's note 'another case is not Zlib' would read better as 'exact matching: only the spelling Zlib is listed'. To my knowledge, the SPDX list id for the zlib/libpng licence with acknowledgement is 'zlib-acknowledgement', with a lowercase z. Vector 7 (line 129) and README.md:43 use 'Zlib-acknowledgement', which is valid but not the canonical spelling; the canonical one is the more realistic near miss. Also from my own knowledge: 'Zlib' is the SPDX id of the zlib License, the licence is OSI-approved, and the README's three conditions match its text.

findings.summary: P2-F1 and P2-F2 are quoted exactly. Their dispositions describe validate_license_amendment_v2.py of packet 242, which is not in this subject, in the present tense.
findings.evidence: In both rows, severity, location, finding and requiredChange equal the strings in the source review-round2.json. The source's round (2), date (2026-10-10) and subject commit cf04fb497dba671199543507b2b7438e132b1609 match. The dispositions answer the findings: a validator-side replay of every A1 and A2 vector (ValueError counts as REFUSED, outcome and elections compared); negative decided cases for an out-of-scope review term, a base denial, an unknown term and open content outside ARTIFACT; and an era-membership check before any read. They are commitments, though. scripts/validate_license_amendment.py (the 223 layer) is unchanged, so both findings still hold for that era. Suggest future-tense wording or an explicit 'verified in the 242 packet review', and use both as acceptance criteria there.

findings.summary: The brief, which will be published, names operator-local state paths (~/.local/state/...).
findings.evidence: REVIEW_BRIEF.md:38 and :46 cite '~/.local/state/harness-onion-ci/tools/...'. They contain no username or other personal data. But they are author-side paths, which amendment.json itself describes as not published on main, and A1's published REVIEW_BRIEF.md has no such paths. Consider 'the author-side review record (not published)' and 'the author-side builder' instead.
